candidates.title: The Question He Answers Badly
candidates.one_line_concept: Aachu asks the fragile question indirectly through normal tiny moments, and Zuv keeps answering with ordinary proof instead of a perfect speech.
candidates.suggested_text_hook: am i hard to love, or just hard to reassure?
candidates.why_people_may_share: The send-trigger is for the partner who does show up but freezes when asked for words. Someone sends it as a softer way of saying, 'I do not need a grand answer, I need proof I can feel.'
candidates.why_people_may_comment: Warm bait: 'this is me asking for reassurance in the worst possible way' and 'he answers by fixing things, not talking.' It invites confession without making either person the villain.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: People in anxious-but-loved relationships will feel caught, then relieved. It says the scary thing without accusing the partner of failing.

candidates.title: Not Too Much, Just Untranslated
candidates.one_line_concept: The carousel reframes 'hard to understand' as two people learning each other's private language: silence, overthinking, checking in, retreating, returning.
candidates.suggested_text_hook: am i hard to understand, or did no one learn my language?
candidates.why_people_may_share: This is a send to the person who finally understands your weird signals: the half-text, the quiet mood shift, the 'nothing' that very much means something.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: Warm bait: 'he knows my face before I say anything' and 'I am fluent in her silence now.' Couples get to brag gently about being known.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: High save energy for people who want to feel less broken. The share is intimate, almost like saying thank you for translating me.

candidates.title: The Risk Was Staying
candidates.one_line_concept: Instead of asking 'am I worth the risk?' the story shows love as the risk of staying soft with someone who has seen your mess and still reaches back.
candidates.suggested_text_hook: what if the risk was letting me be seen?
candidates.why_people_may_share: This travels when one person wants to say, 'thank you for not making me audition for love after I got scared.' It is more sendable than a direct 'am I worth it' because it carries gratitude, not pressure.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: Warm bait: 'being seen is terrifying' and 'this one hurt nicely.' It opens comments from people who are loved well but still flinch.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: A little heavier, more save-forward than tag-forward. Strong for followers who like the brand's quiet cinematic ache.

candidates.title: Handle With Familiar Hands
candidates.one_line_concept: Aachu worries she is hard to handle, but the carousel shows Zuv already knows the tiny care instructions: water by the bed, space after an argument, coming closer without cornering her.
candidates.suggested_text_hook: am i hard to handle, or do i come with instructions?
candidates.why_people_may_share: The tag reason is specific: 'you literally know all my care instructions.' It lets someone thank their partner while teasing themselves for being particular.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: Warm bait: 'mine knows snacks first, questions later' and 'my care label says do not talk to me until I have eaten.' Commenters can name their own instructions.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: This is the lightest, most taggable version of the premise. It turns insecurity into couple folklore instead of a breakup threat.

top_pick.title: The Question He Answers Badly
top_pick.reason: Best send-not-like engine. The first line hooks the insecurity in three seconds, but the payoff can be ordinary proof instead of a therapy quote. It gives both sides dignity: she is not needy, he is not cold, they are just mismatched in reassurance style.
top_pick.send_trigger: A partner sends this when they want reassurance without starting a heavy talk.
top_pick.tag_reason: He may recognize himself as the person who loves through actions but needs help saying the thing out loud.
top_pick.warm_comment_bait: this is me asking for reassurance in the worst possible way

engagement_rationale: The strongest candidates make the follower feel socially safe sending the post. 'Am I hard to love?' by itself can become generic sad-girl wallpaper; the share comes when the carousel names a real couple mechanic: reassurance styles, private languages, fear of being seen, or care instructions. Top pick wins because it creates swipe tension immediately: will he answer wrong, or will the story reveal he has been answering in his own language the whole time?
distribution_risks: If the text stays only in abstract self-worth language, it will earn likes but not sends.
If Zuv is framed as emotionally useless, the send becomes a fight-starter instead of a soft nudge.
If every slide forces both Aachu and Zuv into frame, the story may feel staged instead of intimate; some slides should let absence, objects, or one person's body language carry the point.

If the visuals borrow the concept screenshots' foreign painterly style, the post will feel off-brand; approved direction stays warm off-white watercolor-and-ink with visible paper grain and hand-drawn text later.
If the hook over-explains therapy language, it loses the three-second scroll catch.
